title: Anti-reflection coating
summary: Reduce the reflection from a thick slab of dense glass (n = 2). It reflects about a third of the beam from the left. You may place up to two coating slabs (n = 1.4) in the marked region. The score is how far the reflected power lies below the beam power, in decibels. 10 dB means 10 percent is reflected, 20 dB means 1 percent.
hints: Each face of the glass reflects some light. A thin coating in front of a face adds a second reflection. If the two reflections come back half a wavelength out of step, they cancel.

Light crosses a coating of thickness t twice, so a coating a quarter wavelength thick inside the coating, t = 1 / (4 × 1.4) ≈ 0.18 micrometres, delays its reflection by half a wavelength. Parts may not touch, and the thin air gap between coating and glass adds to the delay. Keep the gap small and make the coating a little thinner.

One coating on the front face cannot remove the reflection from the back face, so place a second coating behind the glass. Coatings 0.13 micrometres thick, 0.06 micrometres away from the glass and as tall as the glass give about 19 dB.

goal.text: Reduce the light reflected by the glass
